description: Full author list of the paper, in publication order, primarily for identifying the publication. Preserve the author string as shown in the paper/metadata rather than abbreviating. Type: free text string with authors separated consistently (the table currently uses semicolon-separated names).
4-digit year of publication of the specific paper entry. Type: integer year as plain text/number, e.g. 2020.
Exact title of the publication. Preserve the paper title, to uniquely identify the study. Type: free text string.
Publication abstract. Prefer the official abstract text; if none is available, leave blank rather than inventing a summary. Type: long free text.
Journal, preprint server, or venue where the work appeared, e.g. Nature Communications, Cell, bioRxiv. Type: short free text label.
Best primary link to the paper. Prefer DOI URL when available; otherwise use the stable publisher/preprint URL. Type: URL string.

Date and optionally time when this entry was added to the bibliography/table, not when the paper was published. Preserve the existing table style if extending the sheet. Type: date-time string in the current table format, e.g. 12/17/2025 18:14.
Dataset identifier for this study in MPRABase. Use the database ID when present (e.g. DS0032). If the paper is not catalogued there, use "not in MPRABase" rather than leaving blank.

Main biological/technical topic of the study, at a coarse level. Use a short controlled label matching the existing style, such as transcription, UTRs, coding, splicing, Software, protocol, or a concise combined label if the study truly spans multiple areas.

Whether the tested library contains deliberately designed/engineered sequences rather than only native sequences. Follow the table's compact convention: "+" = clearly synthetic/engineered design present, "-" = only native or naturally derived sequences, "+/-" = if both kinds were tested.

Main molecular cloning strategy used to build the library backbone or insert library before cell delivery. Use short method labels in lower case, e.g. gibson, restriction, in-fusion, golden gate, or a concise combination if multiple methods were used.

Whether and how library complexity was intentionally bottlenecked during cloning/library propagation to control barcode-per-sequence representation. Record both presence and method when reported, using concise phrases such as "-", "colony scraping", "liquid, max complexity", or "colony counting to estimate coverage". "Max complexity" indicates that the authors did not bottle-neck to restrict the barcodes per sequence, but instead tried to get the highest number or complexity.

Approximate average number of distinct barcodes linked to each tested sequence/variant. Use a plain numeric value when reported. If the assay has no barcode design, use the explicit table convention "no BC".

Short category describing what is being perturbed/tested at the sequence level. Use concise labels matching the table style, e.g. fragments, point, synthetic, random seq, synthetic, binding sites, or a short comma-separated combination where needed.

Species of origin of the biological system or sequence context being assayed. Use short organism labels, e.g. human, mouse, yeast, fly, or a concise combined label if multiple species are central to the assay.

Experimental system in which the assay was performed, typically a cell line, organism, tissue, extract, or other assay context. Use the specific model when possible, e.g. HEK293T, K562, mESC, yeast, explant retina.

Whether the reporter assay readout comes from non-integrated DNA or from genomically integrated constructs. Prefer the controlled values seen in the table: episomal, genomic, both/genomic, episomal if both formats were used, or a very short clarification if the paper is unusual.

Only for episomal/plasmid-based assays: state whether the plasmid backbone contains an origin/promoter-like sequence (Ori) that could influence reporter activity, and note any mitigation used by the authors. Use concise values such as yes, yes but 4x polyA to prevent Ori activity, etc. Leave blank if not applicable or not reported.

For genomically integrated assays, state the mechanism used to insert the reporter library. Use short labels such as Lenti, PB, Bxb1, Cre, homologous recombination, AAV. For non-integrating/episomal assays, use the table's explicit value "none" rather than blank if that is clearly applicable.

Where integrated reporters land in the genome. Use a specific safe-harbor/locus when known (e.g. AAVS1, H11, Hprt, TRP1), "many" for random multi-site integration, or "none" for non-integrating assays when clearly applicable.

Primary assay readout used to quantify activity/effect. Record the measurement modality, not the biological conclusion. Use concise labels matching the table style, e.g. RNA/DNAseq, RNAseq, scRNAseq, FACS+DNAseq, Flow cytometry, RNA.

Promoter used in the reporter construct, especially for transcription-focused assays. Capture the specific promoter identity when stated, not just "minimal promoter" if more detail is available, e.g. minP, minP (pGL4), minRho, SCP1. If the assay tests promoters rather than using one fixed promoter, describe that briefly.

Total number of variants/sequences tested according to the MPRABase entry for this study, only when the paper is in MPRABase. Preserve the database-derived number exactly as a numeric string. Leave blank if unavailable; do not infer from the paper unless it is clearly this database field.

Approximate number of unique tested sequences/construct variants evaluated in the study itself. Use the paper's own scale where possible, as a plain number or simple formatted number string (e.g. 7,800; 120,000). This field is study-centric, not database-centric.
Very short description of the genomic breadth or scope of the tested sequence set. Use labels in the existing style such as genome-wide, one or few loci.

Length in base pairs of the tested variable sequence insert(s). Use the main designed/tested insert length as a plain number when a single dominant length is used. If multiple important lengths are central, use a short explanatory text.

Location of the barcode relative to the reporter construct/transcript. Use concise positional labels such as 5'UTR, 3'UTR, upstream of promoter, in plasmid, DNA, no BC, or a short combination if multiple barcodes are used.
Barcode length in base pairs. Use a plain numeric value when barcodes exist, or the explicit value "no BC" for non-barcoded assays.

Short high-level MPRA/reporter design class. Use one of the established design labels where possible, e.g. plasmidMPRA, lentiMPRA, STARR-seq, CRE-seq, CapStarr-seq, AAV-MPRA, SLOT, FACS-sort + DNAseq.

Typical sequencing depth, filtering threshold, or achieved read coverage per tested sequence/variant or per barcode, if the paper reports it. This can be numeric or short descriptive text, e.g. 100, >=3 RNA counts and >=10 DNA counts per BC, or an estimated RNA/DNA read summary. Leave blank if not reported.

Concise description of how the starting reporter library was physically built before delivery into cells. Include the essential design logic: source of inserts (e.g. microarray-synthesized, genomic fragments), where they were placed relative to promoter/reporter, and how barcodes were coupled if relevant. Type: short prose, usually 1 sentence.

Composition of the input library in terms of sequence classes or controls, if reported. Record approximate fractions or counts of test vs positive/negative control sequences, e.g. ~10% ctrls, ~10% pos, ~10% neg ctrls. Leave blank if not reported.

How the input library itself was sequenced or verified prior to the functional assay, especially for barcode-sequence mapping. Record the essential sequencing/verification approach in short prose, e.g. input plasmid pool sequenced, long read sequencing, PCR with Illumina P5/P7 primers.

How the MPRA/reporter library was introduced into the experimental system. Capture the delivery method and optionally key scale details if they are central, e.g. lipofection, nucleofection, electroporation, lentiviral delivery, or a short prose summary of transfection conditions.

How the RNA-derived sequencing library was prepared during assay readout. Record the major steps in concise protocol language, e.g. RNA extraction, RT, barcode PCR; poly(A) selection, targeted RT, PCR; reporter-specific RT. Use "none" if no RNA library was generated.

How the DNA/input/genomic DNA sequencing library was prepared during assay readout or normalization. Record the major steps in concise protocol language, e.g. plasmid DNA isolation, PCR of BCs; DNA extraction, barcode PCR. Use "none" when appropriate.

Whether unique molecular identifiers were used in RNA/DNA library prep, and if so how/where they were introduced. Use concise values such as no, yes, yes, scRNAseq, yes, reporter-specific RT, yes, added in first PCR.

Very short free-text summary of the assay strategy or special platform aspect that is not already captured by the design-category field. Use this for a compact conceptual label, e.g. STARRseq, dose-response, landing pad + transcriptional reporter, UMI-STARR.

column_name: what predicts activity? (e.g. accessible -> active in MPRA?)
description: Specific statement about features reported to correlate with measured MPRA activity, such as accessibility, histone marks, sequence grammar, or lack of correlation. Capture the result as a short factual note, not a broad interpretation. Leave blank if the paper does not address this.

Short miscellaneous notes that are important for downstream interpretation but do not fit the dedicated columns. Keep this concise and only use it for genuinely relevant information, e.g. unusual caveats, landmark-status notes, integration efficiency, special barcode caveats.

Number of distinct assay conditions in which the same library/sequences were tested, such as different cell types, time points, media, perturbations, or agonist doses. Type: integer count as plain text/number.

Short description of what varied across the conditions counted in the previous column. Use compact labels such as cell types, Agonist concentrations, TF levels, time points neuron diff, species, etc. Leave blank if the study effectively has only one condition or the condition type is not relevant.
